tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

ddqn-mdp-setup: Section IV, p.2: the paper states its DDQN agent and MDP environment as its own method.
state-encoding-matrix: Section IV, p.3: the paper states its own state encoding, shape (M,5N+3). The text then lists four features for the last 3 columns, a paper inconsistency that does not touch the shape.
ddqn-update-and-loss: Eq. (1), p.3, and Algorithm 1 step 2.11.3, p.3: the paper defines its own update rule and loss as printed.
reward-weighted-sum: Section IV.B, Eq. (3), p.4: the paper states its reward and weights 50,30,10,10.
qfi-definition-fixed-theta: Section IV.B.1, Eq. (4), p.4: the paper defines the QFI it uses and fixes theta=pi/2.
entanglement-entropy-definition: Section IV.B.2, Eq. (5), p.4: von Neumann entropy of the reduced state, defined by the paper.
depth-gate-ratio-definitions: Section IV.B.3-4, Eqs. (6)-(7), pp.4-5: the paper defines both ratios, printed without parentheses.
entanglement-boosting-threshold: Section IV.A, p.4: boosting adds gates when entropy falls below the threshold, set to 0.7 (Table 1, p.5, also lists 0.7).
entanglement-injection-pattern: Section IV.A, p.4: the paper defines its injection as an H then CNOT pattern inserted into weakly entangled layers.
network-components-setup: Section IV.A, Eq. (2), pp.3-4, and Section V, p.5: attention, critic layer, entanglement-focused layer and Adam are stated as its own architecture.
training-environment-setup: Section V, p.5: custom OpenAI Gym environment, 2 to 20 qubits, 15 to 160 gates, 1000 episodes, stated by the paper.
simulators-and-initial-circuits: Table 1, p.5 lists AER, state vector; Algorithm 1 step 2.2, p.3 resets to a random or user circuit. All stated setup.
noise-model-setup: Section V, p.6: depolarizing and thermal relaxation errors, built with Qiskit noise model and Aer, stated by the paper.
baseline-choice-and-modification: Section V, pp.5-6: the paper states it chose [7] as baseline and added measuring metrics to make it comparable.
tket-qiskit-merged-passes: Section V, p.9: the paper states it merged Qiskit and Tket passes with custom templates and picked the best circuit by measurements.
future-work-and-mps: Section VI, pp.10-11: the paper's own list of planned work (scalability, error mitigation, PPO, hardware-aware, MPS). Scope statement, not a result.
no-hardware-validation: Section VI, p.10: the paper lists validation on real quantum hardware as future work, so none was done. All experiments are simulation (Table 1, AER).
scaling-limit-20-qubits: Section VI, p.10: the paper states exponential complexity in qubits, simulations to 20 qubits, larger systems challenging. A limit it states about its own work.
scope-two-applications: Section 1.1, p.4: the review states its two chosen applications in its own words.
scope-excludes-ai: Section 1.1, p.5: the wider field of big data and AI is stated as outside the scope, with QML for chemistry and fluids discussed.
scope-excludes-qec-verification: Section 1.1, p.5: QEC, verification and testing (benchmarks excepted, section 2.7) and platform comparisons are stated as having their own reviews.
qaoa-tree-parameter-definition: Abstract p.1 and Section 3 p.4: the paper defines tree parameters as the optimizers of the D-regular tree edge expectation. The abstract says girth at least 2p+1, the body says greater than 2p+1, and the value records both.
qaoa-full-hilbert-setup-20-24-28: Section 3, p.5 and Figure 1 caption: sizes 20, 24, 28, 10 post-selected random 3-regular graphs and 10 bipartite graphs, tree parameters from [WuLy21, Table 1] up to p=11. Stated setup.
qaoa-gw-warm-start-definition: Section 4, pp.6-7, Eqs. (9)-(12): the paper defines the GW warm-start step by step (projection, Bloch circle, product state, mixer).
qaoa-warm-start-p0-three-quarters-bound: Section 4, p.7 states E[cut at p=0] >= 3/4 C_GW and Appendix A, pp.12-13, Eqs. (15)-(22), gives a self-contained proof with its conditions (average over random 2-d plane and axis orientation; non-negative f and g in inequality (20)).
qaoa-large-graph-method-p5: Section 5, p.9 and Appendix B, p.13: the paper states p=5 is the depth reached before the tensor network methods become too costly, and that neighborhood size grows with p, limiting depth.
qaoa-large-graph-setup-64-512: Section 5, p.9 and Figure 4 caption, p.10: ten random 3-regular graphs at n=64,128,256,512, no post-selection, tree parameters, orientation optimized at p=0 for the warm start. Stated setup.
qaoa-no-quantum-advantage-claim: Section 5, p.11: the paper states it does not claim quantum advantage from the warm-start passing the GW line.
qaoa-results-only-for-3-regular-ensemble: Section 1, p.2: the paper states all results concern MaxCut on random 3-regular graphs and it can only speculate beyond that.
qaoa-open-standard-vs-warmstart-high-p: Section 6, p.12: the paper states, from its own Figure 4, that it is unclear whether standard QAOA will surpass warm-start at larger p, and names other problems as open.
qaoa-no-general-guarantee: Abstract p.1 and Section 1 p.2: the paper states its numerics are not proofs and give no general performance guarantee.
qaoa-scope-maxcut-512: Section 6, p.11: restriction to MaxCut on 3-regular graphs up to 512 vertices. The classical-expectation sentence is in the abstract p.1; the stored page label is slightly off but the content is the paper's own scope.
vrp-3node-setup: Section 4.1-4.2, pp.12-14: a random 3-node, 2-vehicle VRP, link-based formulation, depth 2, run on the 127-qubit IBM-Rensselaer machine. Stated setup.
vrp-error-suppression-used: Section 4.2, p.14: dynamic decoupling applied, Pauli twirling also used. Stated setup.
vrp-hardware-qubit-limit: Section 4.4.1, p.17: the paper states the 127-qubit device limits the problem size it can run.
vrp-limitation-circuit-growth: Section 4.6, p.19: the paper states, as its own limitation, that growth in circuit complexity brings decoherence and noise that reduce accuracy. The causal wording is the authors' view, but it is a stated limit.
vrp-conclusion-contribution: Section 5, p.23: the paper states its contribution is an experimental analysis of bottlenecks, not a new algorithm variant.
qaoa-vrp-scalability-limit: Abstract p.1 and Section 4.6, p.19: the paper states scalability remains constrained by circuit complexity and decoherence.
verifiable-definition: Stage I research, Verifiability, p.5: the paper defines 'verifiable' for its own use.
quantumly-verifiable-definition: Verifiability, pp.5-6: defines 'quantumly verifiable'. The independent-reproducibility consequence is stated in the same paragraph, with the example.
verifiability-guiding-principle: Verifiability, p.6 (last paragraph): the paper says its conditions are guiding principles, not an absolute criterion, and that certified randomness may be useful without efficient verification. A caveat on its own proposed criterion.
advantage-speedup-terms: Introduction, 'Focus on finding hard instances', p.2: the paper defines its use of 'advantage' and 'speedup'.
scope-fault-tolerant-speedups: Introduction, p.1: the paper states its focus on computational speedups, mainly for fault-tolerant machines, and sets sensing, metrology and communication aside.
stage0-definition-and-exclusion: The five stages, p.3: the paper describes Stage 0 and states it will not discuss it further.
stage1-definition: The five stages, p.3: the paper defines Stage I.
stage2-definition: The five stages, p.3: the paper defines the advance from Stage I to Stage II.
stage2-verifiable-criterion: Stage II research, p.6: the paper states its own criterion for reaching Stage II, with the super-quadratic ensemble as an example. It adds the condition 'with probability vanishing at most polynomially', which the value omits but does not contradict.
stage2-worst-case-not-enough: The five stages, p.3: the paper states its own rule that worst-case-only speedups are not yet Stage II, with its reason. Repeated in Stage II research, p.6.
stage3-definition: The five stages, pp.3-4: the paper defines Stage III.
stage4-definition: The five stages, p.4: the paper describes Stage IV and its shift to concrete resource costs.
figure1-nonlinear-stages: Figure 1 caption, p.4: the paper states the framework is conceptual, not always linear, with Shor's algorithm covering stages I to III at once.
stage4-substages: Stage IV research, pp.11-12: the paper lists Stage IV(a) to (d). The text layer splits (d) across a page; the next page says 'exact resource counts (up to uncertainties from decoding feedback) as opposed to merely estimates'. The value drops the decoding-feedback caveat but is otherwise as stated.
table4-horizon-classification: Table IV caption, p.14: the paper defines its horizon classes by physical qubit counts at 10^-3 error, with exponents flattened in the text layer. A classification the paper sets for its own table.
babbush-five-stages: kept HIGH at the team lead's decision: the paper's own definition of its framework; team lead, 2026-10-31, Sprint 14 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 28 as recommended)

theory_low.qft-gate-count: Section 2.3.1, p.9 gives only a partial counting sketch (the swap part, floor(3n/2) CNOTs) and then states O(n^2). It is a textbook result in a review, not a derivation in the paper.
theory_low.qaoa-bipartite-locality-upper-bound: Section 4.2, p.8: a prose locality argument (tree neighborhoods w.h.p., so same QAOA cut value) with no theorem, conditions or proof. Informal argument.
theory_low.qaoa-gw-perfect-on-bipartite: Section 4.2, p.8: a short prose argument. The optimal relaxed SDP solution (opposite unit vectors) is asserted, not derived. Informal.
theory_low.qaoa-bipartite-warmstart-p0-optimal: Section 4.2, p.8: a prose argument that follows from the preceding informal claim about the GW solution. No theorem or proof.
theory_low.qaoa-locality-sum-over-edges: Appendix B, p.13: a light-cone argument in prose with Eqs. (23)-(24), no theorem statement or formal proof. It is a standard locality argument used for the method, not a proved result in this paper.
theory_low.eft-amplitude-estimation-vs-sampling: Compilation for early fault-tolerance, p.15: an informal cost argument with no theorem or proof, ending 'a detailed study is required'. The gate counts are stated, not derived. Authors' reasoning.
